survey_report_interpretation: The field report says no new dangers, but final office review digitized a new submerged rock, retained older charted rocks because their actual positions may fall inshore of survey coverage, and accepted small survey holidays and some dynamic-bottom vertical discrepancies. The report supplies no exact new-rock position in its text. Its HCell rocky-seabed areas were generalized at 1:200,000 scale and cannot be used as precise reef edges. This is a survey-level hold until original HCell/current ENC feature geometry and survey gaps are reconciled, not an all-clear for historical camera windows or a navigation route.
survey_fishing_promotion_hold: The original 2 m MLLW BAG overlaps 13 historical rock/cobble camera windows on two July 31, 2010 transects at roughly 41.5–46.0 m MLLW. Nine windows have historical rockfish visual codes; none records lingcod. These correlated observations are not 13 reefs or a present catch estimate. Although the 2009 field report says no dangers, final office review added a submerged rock, retained charted rocks with uncertain inshore positions, and accepted small survey holidays and some dynamic-bottom vertical discrepancies. The text lacks exact new-rock geometry, and HCell rocky-seabed areas were generalized for a 1:200,000 chart. Hold fishing-target promotion until original HCell and current ENC features, actual substrate footprint, MPA/federal exclusions, route, Mendocino date/method rules and harbor access are checked for each candidate area.
